topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, sets out the scope of the cancer lecture course, and outlines the core learning objectives.

topics.label: Determinants of Cancer Risk: Intrinsic Errors versus Environmental Exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer arises from genetic and microenvironmental alterations, debating the relative contributions of random intrinsic errors versus environmental factors supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Biological Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis, Tumor Promotion, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular and cellular mechanisms through which carcinogenic agents and tumor promoters interact with cellular metabolism and host tissues to induce malignant transformation.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify mutational signatures and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of exposures.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture with a concluding summary on environmental carcinogenesis and the everyday appraisal of exposure risks versus benefits.
